items.body:
Australian bootmaker R.M.Williams introduces ‘Worn Well’, starring Australian actor, writer and filmmaker Joel Edgerton, celebrating a life shaped by experience. Built on the belief that character isn’t something you put on, but something earned over time, Worn Well explores the people, places and experiences that leave their mark. Like a well-worn pair of R.M.Williams boots, these stories become richer with time.
Joel Edgerton: a life worn well
A long-time wearer of R.M.Williams boots, Joel shares a genuine connection with the brand. Worn Well features boots from his personal collection alongside new season styles including Craftsman, Yearling, Rigger and Gardener.
“There’s something I really value about things that are made to last. Whether it’s a pair of boots, a piece of work or the relationships you build along the way, time gives things meaning. That idea really resonated with me when it came to Worn Well,” says Joel Edgerton.
“I’ve always respected what R.M.Williams represents, great craftsmanship, longevity and a very Australian sense of identity. Worn Well feltlike a natural fit because it’ s really about celebrating experience and the character we build over time”.
‘Worn Well’ reflects a distinctly Australian approach to style and character, grounded in authenticity, craft and substance; qualities shared by Joel and R.M.Williams and reflected in work designed to stand the test of time.
“Joel was a natural choice for ‘Worn Well’. He brings an authenticity and quiet confidence that strongly reflects the spirit of R.M.Williams. His career has been built on craft, longevity and following his own path, qualities that sit at the heart of this campaign,” says Paul Grosmann, R.M.Williams CEO.
Made for Life
For more than 90 years, R.M.Williams has created products designed to be lived in. From its iconic boots handcrafted in Adelaide to its evolving collections of apparel and accessories, the brand continues to champion durability and timeless Australian design. Made with purpose and designed for longevity, each piece is created to accompany its wearer through everyday moments and defining experiences. A well-worn pair of boots carries the evidence of that journey: the places it has seen and the experiences lived. Marks, creases and patina become part of its story.
‘Worn Well’ brings these principles together to celebrate not simply products, but the lives lived in them. R.M.Williams boots, apparel and accessories are available at stores across Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, and online globally.

He joins from Kingfisher where he was chief AI officer, leading the team which built and scaled […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Morrisons is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Mohsen Ghasempour as chief AI officer.
Ghasempour is an experienced technology leader, with a PHD in computer science and a proven track record of driving AI innovation at enterprise-scale. He joins from Kingfisher where he was chief AI officer, leading the team which built and scaled Kingfisher’s AI function in its operations across Europe. Prior to that, he held senior technology roles at The Hut Group.
In this newly created role Ghasempour will establish a central data science and AI function for Morrisons which will take overall responsibility for Data and AI strategy, with a focus on customer growth; empowering colleagues; operational efficiency; manufacturing excellence; and commercial excellence.
Ghasempour will take up his post on 1 October 2026 and will report to Rami Baitiéh, Morrisons CEO.
Rami Baitiéh, Morrisons CEO, said: “Creation of this new role reflects our commitment to ensuring Morrisons is embracing the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus and in the right way. Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands-on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions that serve customers, empower colleagues and deliver measurable business impact. I’m delighted to welcome him to Morrisons and look forward to his contribution to our growth plans.”
Ghasempour said: “I’m excited about joining Morrisons and building the team that will help the business make effective and responsible use of AI in the years ahead, to deliver real benefits for customers and colleagues.”

items.title: New research: retailers without onsite AI search risk losing shoppers to ChatGPT and Claude
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Fifty nine per cent of US and UK consumers surveyed admit they often leave ecommerce stores because the onsite search is poor. But in addition to leaving to search on Google or a rival online retailer, 40% now say they’re likely to switch to the likes of ChatGPT or Claude when they’re shown irrelevant onsite […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Fifty nine per cent of US and UK consumers surveyed admit they often leave ecommerce stores because the onsite search is poor. But in addition to leaving to search on Google or a rival online retailer, 40% now say they’re likely to switch to the likes of ChatGPT or Claude when they’re shown irrelevant onsite search results. The same number (40%²) also agree that AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude are now more helpful than the onsite search tools offered on many online shopping sites.
The survey of 2,000 US and UK consumers suggests that while shoppers are prepared to try to overcome poor onsite search by rewriting queries or using filters to narrow down the results, a substantial proportion are likely to leave when they see irrelevant results: 62% are likely to go to Google; 53% are likely to go to another shopping website; and 40% are likely to turn to a general AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude (rising to 50% for consumers under 45)³.
The research, which was commissioned by Nosto, the agentic Commerce Experience Platform (CXP), suggests that shoppers are often dissatisfied with the quality of results and the practical difficulties of using onsite search on ecommerce sites.
Tuukka Häkkinen, chief product officer at Nosto, said: “Consumers’ expectations about ecommerce onsite search are likely to have been raised by their experience of using AI assistants. This may explain why four in ten now say they are likely to leave ecommerce stores for the likes of ChatGPT or Claude when they’re not happy with the onsite search results. It’s a wake-up call for retailers to improve their search or risk driving shoppers away.”
The frustrations shoppers say they come up against ‘often’ aren’t just about irrelevant results. The data suggests that traditional onsite search forces them to do too much work. As well as the results not matching what they typed (64%), shoppers complain about being shown too many results to scroll through (search overload) (70%); the struggle of finding the right words to describe what they want (62%); and the same products being listed even after changing the search terms over and over (66%)¹.
| What frustrates shoppers most about onsite search? | % | 
| GETTING THE QUERY RIGHT |  | 
| I have to use very specific, exact terms | 70% | 
| I know what I want but can’t find the words | 62% | 
| I’ve seen a photo of it but can’t describe it | 61% | 
| TOO MUCH TO SIFT THROUGH |  | 
| There are way too many results to scroll through | 70% | 
| The whole process takes too long | 61% | 
| RESULTS THAT MISS |  | 
| I keep seeing the same products over and over | 66% | 
| The filters are too generic | 65% | 
| Results show items that don’t match what I typed | 64% | 
Many of these frustrations are because traditional onsite search is not able to understand shopper intent, a problem which AI is better at handling according to Tuukka Häkkinen:
“Shoppers often struggle to find the precise words to describe what they’re searching for–at times, they might have only a vague idea. In fashion, for example, someone might be looking for ‘a smart casual outfit for a summer wedding’, rather than searching for a very specific product.
“AI is better able to address this type of query because it goes beyond simple keyword matching – by understanding more natural conversational language and descriptions. And by asking follow-up questions, AI can help narrow down options. It’s got the potential to make product discovery easier, quicker and less frustrating.”
Shoppers are ready for retailers to bring AI into onsite search
The good news for online retailers is that most shoppers are receptive to AI being used directly on retail sites to enhance onsite search; 72% have already tried or would be open to retailers using AI to improve search on their sites. 63%⁴ agree it would help if an AI assistant helped them refine or improve their search query on a retail site by asking additional questions to clarify what they are looking for.
Among consumers who have already used AI-powered onsite search on retail shopping sites, more than 95% believe AI search technology can be helpful in a variety of ecommerce sectors or types of purchase. The ecommerce sectors where they see AI being most helpful are Electronics and Appliances (33%) and Clothing and Fashion (32%), followed by Groceries and Everyday Essentials (29%), and Beauty and Skincare (25%).
When Nosto’s survey asked consumers what they would want or expect if retailers introduced AI to improve onsite search, many answers matched the frustrations they highlighted about traditional ecommerce search. As well as wanting AI to help them find products faster (34%), they want it to narrow down choices (30%), to understand what they mean even when their search queries are not clear (27%); show fewer, more relevant products instead of long lists of less relevant results (26%); and to guide them by suggesting products when they’re unsure about what they want (24%).
| What shoppers want/ expect from AI if it was introduced to improve ecommerce onsite search | % | 
| Helps me find products I am looking for faster | 34% | 
| Helps me narrow down choices when there are too many options | 30% | 
| Gives me the option to use AI or not use AI | 29% | 
| Understands what I am searching for even when I can’t describe it clearly | 27% | 
| Shows me a smaller number of highly relevant products that closely match what I am looking for (rather than more results that also include less relevant products) | 26% | 
| Guides me and gives me ideas to help me find products I might like, when I’m not entirely sure what I want | 24% | 
| Lets me search using a photo instead of words | 22% | 
Consumers’ main concerns about retailers using AI to improve onsite search relate to privacy, control, and transparency. 73% are concerned that stores will track and collect their personal data to train AI; 71% that AI will recommend products to increase retailer profits rather than focusing on what’s best for shoppers; and 69% that shoppers will be forced to use AI without being able to switch back to traditional search. 69% are also concerned that AI features will interrupt and distract them while they shop⁵.
| Shoppers’ concerns about retailers introducing AI to improve onsite search | % | 
| The online store will track my personal data, shopping habits, online behaviors, and uploaded photos to train their AI (Privacy and data tracking) | 73% | 
| AI will push certain products because they are more profitable for the online store rather than being the best choice for me | 71% | 
| I’ll be forced to use AI to search without an option to switch back to traditional search | 69% | 
| AI features constantly pop up, interrupt, and distract me while I am shopping (Screen clutter) | 69% | 
| AI will wrongly assume what I like based on my previous shopping or browsing behavior | 68% | 
| The AI will limit my choices by hiding some items in search results that I might otherwise have considered | 67% | 
| AI will misinterpret my words and show irrelevant products | 65% | 
According to Häkkinen, retailers will need to earn shoppers’ trust by being clear about when their data is being used to improve AI-powered search, what data is involved and why. They should also be given the ability to turn the AI experience on or off. The ideal product discovery experience should use AI in several ways, he said:
“First, AI can work in the background to make search better by understanding less precise queries and returning more relevant results. On top of that, agentic capabilities can proactively help shoppers refine those results, for example by asking follow-up questions, or automatically applying relevant filters, all without getting in the shopper’s way and with the option to undo or turn off these actions. And when shoppers want more help, they should be able to trigger a chat with an AI shopping agent for a more guided conversational experience.”
“Personalisation technology can be used to ensure that AI-powered search results are even more relevant to individual shoppers. By prioritising products that best meet shoppers’ needs, personalization also helps deliver the best results for the retailers’ business.”
Download the full survey report from Nosto at: https://www.nosto.com/blog/ai-search-in-ecommerce-consumer-expectations-readiness/

Beloved British clothing brand Boden has partnered with the world’s most comfortable underwear and sleepwear brand Stripe & Stare on a limited-edition capsule, launching globally on both websites from Sunday 11th October. The very first collaboration between the two brands, it brings together the legendary comfort and cut that Stripe & Stare are loved for, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Beloved British clothing brand Boden has partnered with the world’s most comfortable underwear and sleepwear brand Stripe & Stare on a limited-edition capsule, launching globally on both websites from Sunday 11th October. The very first collaboration between the two brands, it brings together the legendary comfort and cut that Stripe & Stare are loved for, with the print and colour that makes Boden unique. Boden’s ethos is happiness you can wear, and what better way to bring that to life than by starting with underwear that looks great, and feels luxurious?
A nine-piece edit with original and high-rise knickers, thongs, bralettes and a cosy lace cami, the capsule heroes one of Boden’s archival wildflower prints alongside nostalgic stripes and hearts crafted with Stripe & Stare’s cloud-soft TENCEL™ fabric and contrast lace trims. Each piece is a way to bring joy to getting dressed everyday.
“We are so proud to be partnering with the icon that is Boden. Taking their signature stripes and florals and adding them to our hero knickers, camis and bras felt like the most natural thing in the world,” shares Katie Lopes, co-founder and CEO of Stripe & Stare. “They are the home of British stripes, and we love stripes so much they’re even in our name. The stars of the S&S range in Boden’s most-loved prints – we hope you love this collection as much as we do.”
“It’s so exciting to be collaborating with Stripe & Stare on this limited-edition range. There had to be stripes, of course, and the floral print we’ve used was hand-picked from our archive. It’s a vintage motif, reminiscent of a traditional British style, which was then coloured up in-house.” adds Ann Ceprynski, Head of Print Womenswear at Boden.
The launch also coincides with the early days of the festive gift season. Combining everyday practicality with delightful designs, they’re the perfect way to bring a little self-care to whoever the recipient may be. Big prints now come in small packages.

items.body:
Cécred, the renowned haircare line from Beyoncé Knowles-Carter has launched exclusively in the UK with Space NK to a fanfare and record-breaking performance.
Cécred, beloved for transforming all hair types and textures broke the record for the biggest brand launch ever at Space NK – with thousands flocking to store and to spacenk.com to shop the brand in the UK for the first time. The brand met its full week’s predicted sales by 1.1-00pm on launch day and went on to smash previous launch day performance for a new brand.
Stand out products for the collection include the Restoring Hair & Edge Drops (currently the best seller) followed by the latest launch Temple Oud Hair Perfume.
Sophie Wayman, category director, haircare, at Space NK, explains: “We could not be more thrilled with the performance of Cécred, we expected the brand to resonate with our customers, but the demand is truly unprecedented. At 8.30am on launch day we could already see a deluge of search and immediate sales and we think this will only continue”.
“The UK has been our largest market outside the US since day one,” says Grace Ray, CEO of Cécred, “but to mark the biggest launch in Space NK’s history is a true testament to the connection we’ve built with our global community.”
Cécred is available in all 90 Space NK stores and spacenk.com from 22nd September.

Launching from mid-September, the refreshed PureOaty identity brings a clearer and more distinctive look to the […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Glebe Farm Foods is unveiling a refreshed brand identity for its PureOaty drink range, alongside the launch of its new PureOaty Coconut Oat Drink, marking the next stage in the brand’s ambition to become Britain’s leading oat food company.
Launching from mid-September, the refreshed PureOaty identity brings a clearer and more distinctive look to the range, putting taste, trust, transparency and British provenance at the heart of the premium challenger brand.
Under the new strapline ‘Delicious oats. Made simply.’, the refreshed packaging is designed to deliver greater shelf impact while making it easier for shoppers to navigate the range and choose the right product for different usage occasions, helping drive both first-time and repeat purchase.
At the heart of the brand is Glebe Farm Foods’ belief that great taste starts with better oats. Produced using 100% British oats grown on a family farm and by trusted British growers, then milled and manufactured in Cambridgeshire, PureOaty benefits from complete control from field to finished product. Certified gluten free by Coeliac UK, it offers consumers a trusted dairy alternative without compromising on taste.
A fresh twist on oat drinks
Launching alongside the refreshed identity is PureOaty Coconut Oat Drink, combining 15% British gluten free oats with real coconut cream to create a naturally creamy drink with a subtle coconut flavour.
While many coconut drinks use rice or soya as their base, PureOaty’s new recipe combines British gluten free oats and real coconut cream, offering a genuinely different take on the category. Made with just four simple ingredients – water, oats, coconut cream and salt – it contains no gums, stabilisers, flavours or added sugars.
The new Coconut Oat Drink brings together two important plant-based segments, giving consumers a fresh, tropical twist on the oat drinks they already know and enjoy. Coconut is the second-largest plant-based alternative, growing volume sales by 3% in the last 52 weeks, while oat leads the way at 4.8%.
Delicious served chilled, blended into smoothies and shakes, mixed into cocktails and mocktails, or added to coffee, PureOaty Coconut Oat Drink offers a versatile choice for a range of everyday occasions.
Philip Rayner, MD and co-founder of Glebe Farm Foods, said: “Today’s consumers want more from the food and drink they buy. They’re looking for products that deliver on taste, quality and nutrition, made with simple ingredients.
“Because we grow, mill and manufacture our oats ourselves, alongside working with trusted British growers, we know exactly what goes into every carton. That control is central to what we do and helps us deliver the quality and consistency our customers know and love.”
PureOaty Coconut Oat Drink launches on 16 September 2026 and is currently available to purchase through the Glebe Farm Foods website and Amazon, sold in cases of six for £12.30. The rest of the PureOaty oat drink range is available to purchase through the Glebe Farm Foods website, Morrisons, foodservice and retail partners, as well as Amazon.

items.body:
RivingtonHark, on behalf of Rochdale Borough Council, has secured British clothing retailer Peacocks on a long-term lease for a 10,181 sq ft unit at Rochdale Riverside, taking the scheme to 92% occupancy.
The run of new lettings follows a 15.3% year-on-year footfall increase at Rochdale Riverside, with almost 200,000 visiting during July, continuing an upward year-on-year trend throughout 2026.
Following its opening in Spring 2020, Rochdale Riverside has delivered a dynamic mix of shopping, dining, and leisure and is at the heart of the wider regeneration of Rochdale town centre. RivingtonHark has asset managed the centre on behalf of the council since 2023.
The 200,000sq ft open-air scheme is anchored by a 50,000sq ft M&S store and a six-screen Real Cinema, and is home to leading national retailers including Next, H&M, Boots, and JD Sports.
Ollie Holland, asset manager for Rochdale Riverside at RivingtonHark, said: “The letting brings another nationally recognised retailer to Rochdale Riverside, activating a prominent, centrally located unit and further strengthening the diverse and growing fashion offer. The addition of Peacocks reflects robust demand for well situated space and continued confidence from national and regional occupiers in the long-term appeal of Rochdale Riverside.
“Rochdale Riverside is another example of how we work closely with local authorities like Rochdale Borough Council to deliver long-term value across town and city centre schemes. With footfall continuing to grow and further lettings in the pipeline we look forward to building on this continued momentum.”
Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “It’s great to see Rochdale Riverside going from strength to strength with another new store signing up. I’m sure Peacocks will prove to be a popular addition to this busy and well-loved shopping and leisure centre.”
Established in Warrington in 1884 and now trading from 345 stores nationally, Peacocks brings a budget friendly, everyday proposition which adds to the diverse retail mix.
Peacocks is scheduled to open at the start of October and will trade across both ground and first floor levels.

items.title: Dr. Martens unveils new global brand platform ‘With Bouncing Soles’
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. A new chapter for the brand begins on 24 September, bringing together a renewed focus on Dr. Martens’ Icons, a global talent campaign, cultural programming anchored in ‘micro-joys’ and genres of fandom around the world, and a new series of designer collaborations. Launching across four key expressions – a renewed focus on the Icons, a […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
A new chapter for the brand begins on 24 September, bringing together a renewed focus on Dr. Martens’ Icons, a global talent campaign, cultural programming anchored in ‘micro-joys’ and genres of fandom around the world, and a new series of designer collaborations.
Launching across four key expressions – a renewed focus on the Icons, a global campaign featuring die-hard Doc’s wearers, a programme of cultural experiences, and the ongoing Statements in Craft designer collaboration series – the With Bouncing Soles platform celebrates the people and passions that have shaped Dr. Martens for more than six decades, while creating new ways for a generation of wearers to make the brand their own.
With Bouncing Soles arrives dressed for the occasion. An evolved logo, a new typeface, a refined palette and a rebuilt website give the platform a visual identity of its own.
There’s a word that keeps coming up when you spend time inside the world of Dr. Martens. Not iconic, though that too, but enduring. The 1460 boot that rolled off the production line in Wollaston in 1960 is still instantly recognisable. The yellow welt stitch is still there. The air-cushioned sole still bounces. What has changed, constantly, is who is wearing them. And why.
Because Dr. Martens has never really been about just footwear. Across generations, its boots and shoes have become part of people’s lives: the musician who needed armour, the postie who needed support, the teenager who spotted someone else wearing the same pair and instantly thought, you too. That sense of recognition and belonging has always been part of the Dr. Martens story.
At the heart of With Bouncing Soles is one question: “What Makes Your Sole Bounce?”
The campaign name itself has been hiding in plain sight for 65 years. With Bouncing Soles has appeared on the heel loop of every 1460 boot since 1960, originally as a reference to the brand’s air-cushioned sole. Now, those three words become the creative thread connecting Dr. Martens’ heritage with its future – and the generations of people who have given the brand its meaning.
“With Bouncing Soles has been stitched into some of our most iconic boots and shoes since production started in 1960. Today it becomes the creative thread that connects the people who have shaped Dr. Martens with a new generation discovering the brand for themselves. It’s an invitation for people to celebrate creativity, individuality and the confidence to express who they are. What makes a bouncing sole? In some ways, taking the time to ask is just as important as the answer.” – Neil Cummings, Global Brand Creative Director
THE FACES OF WITH BOUNCING SOLES
The AW26 campaign features Chloë Sevigny, Jordan Stephens and Naomi Watanabe, alongside a wider cast of community voices and cultural changemakers, including UK rapper LedByHer.
These aren’t people chosen simply to represent Dr. Martens. They are genuine wearers, each with their own answer to “What Makes Your Sole Bounce?” – the creative obsession, deep interest or personal pursuit they would follow whether anyone was watching or not.
For Jordan Stephens, that answer is language: the pursuit of finding the words that can communicate something true, and the fleeting feeling of being understood. For LedByHer, it’s her devotion to her hometown and the people in it. Each story is told in their own words, on their own terms.
“I’ve worn Dr. Martens at different moments throughout my life, so being part of this campaign feels genuinely authentic. What makes my sole bounce? Words. They continue to open up new ways of seeing, feeling and understanding the world. I love that the campaign plays with the idea of sole and soul because creativity often lives in those layers of meaning. Dr. Martens has always been a symbol of individuality and self-expression, and I’m proud to support a platform that celebrates the people and spaces keeping culture alive.” – Jordan Stephens
“I’ve always been drawn to pieces that become more personal the longer you live in them, and Dr, Martens has always represented that for me. I love that the campaign starts with such a simple question: What Makes Your Sole Bounce? For me, it’s staying curious – taking on new roles, finding inspiration in unexpected places, and always being open to what’s next.” – Chloë Sevigny
ICONS, REIMAGINED
At the heart of the product story are five of Dr. Martens’ most recognisable silhouettes – the 1460 boot, 1461 shoe, Adrian loafer, 2976 Chelsea boot and 8065 Mary Jane – reimagined in Crazy Horse leather, including a new Cherry Red finish for AW26. The 1460, 1461 and 8065 Mary Jane will also be available in new DM’s Green editions.
Known for developing character over time, Crazy Horse leather embodies the idea at the heart of the platform: no two stories, or pairs, are ever the same. Every wearer leaves their mark, with the leather evolving alongside them.
EVENTS AND ‘MICRO-JOYS’ ACROSS THE COUNTRY
With Bouncing Soles is designed, fundamentally, as a platform for participation – events with in-built ‘bounce’ will be staged around the world. In the UK, the programme opens at the Dr. Martens store on Brewer Street in London’s Soho, which becomes a working cultural space for the weeks that follow.
Lala Books, the independent bookshop from Camberwell, installs an honesty library co-curated with Jordan Stephens, and returns in October to host a book club. Poetry collective Adult Entertainment stages an intergenerational dub poetry night. So Young magazine teaches the near-lost craft of the fanzine – cut, stick, copy, bind. Steeze Factory takes the store over for a night of live cyphers, SNL anchor Paddy Young turns the store into a comedy club for a night, and three Substack writers open their notebooks for one-to-one clinics with anyone hoping to make a living from words.
In October the programme travels north to Manchester, where craft and community hub Altogether Otherwise opens ‘Suddenly Real’, a free drop-in poster shop for the city’s makers – made possible by Doc’s, and subculture zine Dance Policy stages ‘The Manchester Bounce’ – a day and a night tracing the city’s soundsystem history through exhibition, conversation and a club floor, all at beloved nightlife venue SOUP. STATEMENTS IN CRAFT
Collaboration has been part of the Dr. Martens story since the very first boot; a meeting of two German doctors and a British bootmaker that produced something none of them could have made alone.
Statements in Craft continues that tradition, bringing together British-based fashion innovators to explore craft, process and what happens when distinct creative identities collide with an icon. The series begins with MHL., Sage Nation, Chopova Lowena and LABRUM.
THE STORY CONTINUES
With Bouncing Soles isn’t a campaign with an end date. It is an ongoing question that will continue through future collections, collaborations, retail experiences and cultural moments.
The question stays the same.
The answers keep changing.

items.title: Amanda Holden sofa range lifts DFS as profit jumps
items.summary: DFS has toasted its partnership with media personality Amanda Holden as the sofa seller saw profits jump by a third.  The London-listed furniture store said its collaboration with the Britain’s Got Talent judge, which includes a range of three Amanda Holden-branded sofas, has lifted its performance. Steve Johnson, chairman of DFS, said that its partnership [...]
items.body:
Amanda Holden sofa range lifts DFS as profit jumps
DFS has toasted its partnership with media personality Amanda Holden as the sofa seller saw profits jump by a third.
The London-listed furniture store said its collaboration with the Britain’s Got Talent judge, which includes a range of three Amanda Holden-branded sofas, has lifted its performance.
Steve Johnson, chairman of DFS, said that its partnership with Holden “has ensured our brands remain at the forefront of the consumer’s mind”.
The retailer’s exclusive brand partnerships “continued to resonate” with consumers despite a “subdued demand environment,” the group told shareholders.
DFS’ Amanda Holden range features three sofas: the ‘showstopper,’ the ‘luvvie’ and the ‘olivier’.
“Amanda Holden knows a thing or two about star quality, and this sofa collection is no exception. Each piece in the range oozes glamorous, thoughtful detail,” the sofa seller’s listing for the range says.
DFS posted a 2.6 per cent uplift in revenue to £1bn in the year to June, as its pre-tax profit grew by a third to £43.7m.
Tim Stacey, the group’s chief executive, said: “Upholstered furniture remains the economic engine of the DFS Group.
“Our goal is to protect and extend our clear leadership position in sofas by penetrating underserved customer segments and geographies, expanding exclusive brand partnerships, and sharpening the proposition, range architecture, and customer experience.”
DFS ‘winning market share from all corners’
The furniture retailer also owns sofa brand Sofology, which posted a 2.9 per cent increase in aisles to £306m, outperforming the two per cent growth notched by the core DFS brand.
DFS told shareholders it is also aiming to boost sales of beds, mattresses and dining room furniture as it targets a £5bn share of the home market.
The group said it is also hoping to grow the Sofa Delivery Company, its logistics operation, after allowing third-party retailers to use it for their deliveries for the first time.
DFS said it received “very positive feedback and [has] launched a dedicated portal to seamlessly onboard future partners”. The Sofa Delivery Company delivered £800,000 in sales in the year, the firm said.
The group said it weathered the falling high street footfall caused by the summer’s heatwaves and reiterated its plans to hit £1.4bn revenue in the medium term.
Analysts at Panmure Liberum said DFS delivered “strong” margin performance, adding that the retailer is “in one of its strongest positions to date”.
“There is a lot to like about how DFS is winning market share from all comers. The move into home items gives another growth angle, and we see no reason why it should not achieve its long-term sales and margin targets,” analysts at Peel Hunt said.

items.body:
Royal Mail inks deal to boosts UK out of home network with acquisition of Quadient parcel lockers
Royal Mail has announced the acquisition of Quadient’s UK-based parcel locker network. Around 3,000 lockers will now become part of Royal Mail’s out of home network. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the calendar year. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “Together with our existing lockers, parcel shops and parcel postboxes, this acquisition will further enhance our out of home network of 30,000 parcel points and strengthen our proposition for customers. This is an exciting step forward in making it even easier for customers to send, collect and return parcels in the way that suits them best, through lockers, shops and other convenient locations.”
The deal strengthens Royal Mail’s position and makes it a major player in a crowded UK parcel lockers market that also includes InPost, Amazon, and YEEP!
SPAR
Earlier this month, Quadient announced a partnership with James Hall & Co., SPAR UK’s primary retailer, wholesaler, and distributor for the North of England.
Parcel Pending by Quadient lockers are being rolled out across James Hall & Co.’s G&E Murgatroyd company owned retail estate, with 37 locations already live and further deployments planned across its network of stores. These offer 24/7 access for deliveries, returns, exchanges, and item storage. They support a range of services, including prescription collection, Click & Collect, key exchange, and spare parts retrieval.
“Through the company’s SPAR stores, partnering with James Hall & Co. allows us to further embed our open locker network into the fabric of local communities across the North of England,” said Katia Bourgeais-Crémel, EVP Parcel Locker Solutions Europe at Quadient. “Convenience retail plays a critical role in everyday life, and by introducing smart, secure lockers into these locations, we are removing friction from parcel collection and returns. This partnership reflects our focus on delivering predictable, scalable last-mile solutions that benefit the entire ecosystem from carriers and retailers to consumers and store staff.”
Fiona Drummond, Company Stores Director at James Hall & Co., said: “We are committed to enhancing the role our SPAR stores play within local communities, offering services that go beyond traditional retail. Partnering with Quadient enables us to introduce a secure and convenient parcel solution that meets the evolving needs of our customers, while driving additional footfall and value for our stores. We look forward to continuing the roll-out across our estate.”
Quadient’s locker network now spans the US, Japan, and Europe, with over 28,200 units installed globally and plans to reach 40,000 by 2030.

Alberto Carlos Benigno named x-hoppers CEO as retail comms firm announces Ace Hardware partnership
Alberto Carlos Benigno has taken on the role of CEO at retail communication specialist x-hoppers. He joined the company in 2025 as Chief Revenue Officer and his CV also includes a stint at x-hoppers owner Wildix and Gartner.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “What better way to mark one of the most significant milestones of my professional life than at the signing of an equally significant strategic partnership: with Ace Hardware, the world's largest hardware cooperative, here in Orlando, Florida, at one of their events.”
He added: “x-hoppers is increasingly becoming the go to solution for retailers worldwide looking to lift productivity through communication technology that makes the entire associate and customer journey frictionless. The data backs it up. I'm incredibly proud of the entire x-hoppers team, who has built this company into a genuine authority in retail technology, and grateful to the Wildix board and the wider company for the opportunity and the trust they place in us every day. Here's to many more milestones ahead: bringing retail to the next level.”
So hot right now
x-hoppers is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…

items.summary: JD Sports Fashion, which often collaborates with TV personalities such as Maya Jama (pictured), said it was operating against a 'tough global consumer backdrop'.
items.body:
JD Sports blames the cost-of-living crisis hitting young people as sales and profits fall
JD Sports has blamed cost of living pressures for weaker spending by younger shoppers as it reported lower sales and profits.
The sportswear chain said it was operating against a ‘tough global consumer backdrop’ – particularly in the US.
Sales totalled £5.9billion for the six months to August 1, down 0.7 per cent on the same period a year ago.
The High Street retailer, which often collaborates with TV personalities such as Maya Jama, also revealed its pre-tax profit, adjusted for one-off items, fell by a fifth to £282million.
JD Sports has previously cautioned over higher inflation eating into consumers wallets, particularly from higher fuel prices.
It flagged weaknesses in the footwear market with fewer big launches from its brand partners coupled with lower confidence to spend among its core demographic of customers, typically aged between 16 and 24.
JD Sports Fashion, which often collaborates with TV personalities such as Maya Jama (pictured), said it was operating against a 'tough global consumer backdrop'
The firm has previously cautioned over higher inflation eating into consumer budgets, particularly from higher fuel prices.
However, it highlighted good momentum for running trainers and clothing and newer styles of shoes.
Chief executive Regis Schultz said the retailer had showed a 'resilient performance against a challenging backdrop of consumer cost-of-living pressures, footwear product cycle headwinds and a highly promotional market'.
JD Sports cut its profit outlook last month, saying it was expecting pre-tax profits for the full year to be between £700million and £800million, down from a previously guided range of £750million to £850million.
It had 4,766 stores worldwide in August – meaning its chain of shops has been reduced by more than 100 since the same time last year.
Experts said JD Sports' trading is impacted by weaker sales trends affecting sportswear giant Nike.
Victoria Scholar, head of investment at Interactive Investor, said: 'The struggles at Nike also have a knock-on effect on JD Sports as one of its most significant brand partners.
'The sportswear giant has fallen out of fashion amid fickle consumers who no longer see Nike products as highly desirable.
'Preferences have shifted towards newer, more exciting, nimble brands like On and Hoka, hurting the longstanding market leaders.'
Shares in the firm yesterday slumped 5.7 per cent, or 4.5p, to 74.22p.

items.body:
Majestic, the UK’s largest specialist wine retailer, has unveiled its first-ever digital loyalty scheme as it continues to invest in making its multichannel proposition even more seamless and convenient for customers.
The loyalty programme forms part of Majestic’s new smartphone app, which is available to download now via the Apple Store and Google Play Store. The app allows customers to discover, shop and earn rewards, with loyalty points able to be redeemed in exchange for free bottles of wine in Majestic stores.
Customers who download the app and sign in or create a Majestic account will receive 50 free points – the equivalent of spending £50. Users will then earn 1 point for every £1 they spend, whether they choose to shop in-store, online, via the app or through a Wine Club or Lock It In subscription. Members can redeem their points exclusively through the app after reaching 100, 200, 400, 800 or 1,600 points, which can then be exchanged for free products in-store. Customers will have a choice of rewards at each tier, ranging from wines in Majestic’s popular Guv’nor family for 200 points, to premium options including E. Guigal Châteauneuf-du-Pape or Lanson ‘Le Black Creation’ Brut Champagne for 1,600 points.
Users can access their digital loyalty cards directly through the app in the form of a unique barcode, which can also be added to their smartphone’s e-wallet in a couple of simple clicks. Customers can also scan their unique barcode in stores, making the physical checkout journey quicker and easier for all shoppers with a Majestic profile.
The new Majestic app will also feature a host of other functionality, allowing customers to build product wishlists and save tasting notes and star ratings for wines, beers and spirits they have previously purchased. Majestic has also made its popular Shop Local functionality available on the app, allowing customers to search the stock available at their local Majestic store, in real-time, for next-day delivery or click-and-collect in as little as four hours. Majestic’s unique Shop Local proposition now accounts for more than half of all orders placed through majestic.co.uk.
Majestic plans to invest further in developing and enhancing the app ahead of the key Christmas trading period and over the coming years, to ensure customers continue to benefit from a seamless multichannel shopping experience.
Elizabeth Newman, managing director of Majestic Retail, said: “We have an incredibly loyal, knowledgeable and highly engaged customer base at Majestic, and we are always looking for new ways to recognise and reward that support. Our first-ever digital loyalty scheme and new smartphone app will make it quicker, easier and more rewarding than ever for customers to discover and buy new wines at Majestic.
“By earning points on every order, whether you are shopping online, in-stores, or signed up to one of our subscriptions, we’re rewarding all of our customers, whenever and however they choose to shop with Majestic. And I can’t think of a better way to thank our customers than by exchanging their points for free bottles of wine, giving them another opportunity to enjoy an old favourite, or discover something new.”
The new Majestic app is available to download now on Apple and Android devices.

Google Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/

items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Today marks the launch of the first stage of the new platform. The initiative sees Sainsbury’s come together with GXO, Greencore, Tesco, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
A new tech solution that brings together logistics providers, retailers and manufacturers is hoping to save food redistribution charity, Felix, millions of pounds in transportation costs, and transform how the sectors work together. Today marks the launch of the first stage of the new platform.
The initiative sees Sainsbury’s come together with GXO, Greencore, Tesco, M&S and Gist. With early support from BCG and Baringa, the group has developed and is trialling the new technology which acts as a ‘mission control’, matching surplus food that needs to be delivered to charities, with spare space on lorries, already travelling across the country. The AI allows it to be both tailored and nimble.
The transformative platform goes beyond transportation, enabling shared visibility of spare factory line capacity, raw ingredients, packaging opportunities, and more, so even more surplus food can reach charities through partnerships across the food industry.
Eight million people go hungry in the UK, 2.1 million of them children according to the Food Foundation, yet most frontline charities say they can’t meet demand for food. The new platform hopes to address this. The project is being led by Alliance Food Sourcing (AFS), a coalition of over 50 leading food companies, convened by Felix and the Institute of Grocery Distributors (IGD).
Speed dating for trucks: how it works
Felix (formerly The Felix Project and FareShare) is the UK’s leading food distribution charity and supports more than 8,000 charities and community groups. In 2025, it spent over £5.6 million on logistics, moving 80,000 pallets to 33 distribution centres.
At the same time, approximately 30% of all HGV journeys have spare capacity, according to the Department for Transport. The new technology aims to close this gap, matching Felix food deliveries with spare space on lorries, to get more surplus food to people who need it.
Early trials on track to generate £170,000 in cost savings
Trials with just two partners – Sainsbury’s and GXO – are on track to move 5,300 tonnes of food, save 42,885 road miles and 62.9 tonnes of CO₂, and deliver £170,000 in cost savings, in just six months. Once scaled up across the food industry, it will cut food waste, transport costs and the number of vehicles on the road, ensuring a more efficient distribution of food to charities. It’s also expected to lead to more offers of surplus food by organisations, due to the enhanced access to transportation.
Calling on the food industry to join
AFS is now calling on more food and logistics businesses to join the initiative as it expands trials across the country.
The model will be tested further over the next six months, with the potential to save Felix £1 million in the first full year of rollout.
Partner activity so far
- Sainsbury’s and GXO are offering free consultancy and logistics support – they’ve identified 10 routes for moving Felix food, with estimated savings of around £170,000 over 6 months.
- Greencore is already providing twice-weekly movements within London, free of charge, with projected annual savings of around £18,000.
- Tesco is providing free consultancy to the project.
- M&S and Gist have committed to providing free consultancy and logistics support.
Simon Roberts, CEO of Sainsbury’s, said: “We believe partnership is key to driving positive change. Our ambitious trial with GXO aimed to optimise our combined transportation networks and reduce the costs involved in distributing food for the incredible charities tackling food insecurity. In our trial alone, we’re looking at charity savings of £170,000. With more businesses coming on board, the potential to scale this up is significant, helping charities direct more of their resources where they matter most, to get more food to people facing hunger.”
Richard Smith, director of food innovation at Felix, said: “This is a really innovative piece of work. Transportation costs Felix millions of pounds a year, and since the conflict in Iran these have risen substantially. Yet these are costs we cannot cut; we need to get the food in and then back out to the over 8,000 charities and community organisations we support. Without our logistics, this food would never reach the millions who need it most. To know this new tech could save so much money is phenomenal, and I want to say a huge thank you to everyone who has helped so far.”
Gavin Williams, CEO of GXO UK & Ireland, said: “We’re proud to support a project that helps get more food to people who need it while reducing waste across the supply chain. By bringing together organisations, technology and logistics expertise, this initiative shows how existing transport networks can be used in smarter ways to create meaningful social impact. We’re pleased to be contributing our operational knowledge and transport capabilities to help build a scalable solution that benefits charities and communities across the UK.”
Darren Binns, head of logistics, Greencore said: “It’s brilliant to see the industry coming together to tackle such an important issue, and we’re proud that Greencore can play a part. By making use of spare capacity on our HGV fleet, we can help get more surplus food to charities while reducing transport costs. It’s a simple idea, but one that shows how technology can help the industry go further to make a real difference.”
Nicky Robinson, drector of AFS, said: “AFS brings different businesses together to collaborate and find joint solutions. This new AI-driven tech is a great example of that – matching offers of surplus food with space in lorries and logistics expertise, to get more food to frontline charities more efficiently. We believe the new platform could save up to £1 million of charity costs in the first year of rollout, and we’d love to have even more food and logistics businesses join us, to scale it up further.”
The initiative supports the Government’s National Programme to redistribute surplus food, which aims to triple charitable food redistribution over the next decade.
As every organisation’s network is different, the prototype platform is being co-designed by businesses for ease of use regardless of systems, and around two main types of transport opportunity:
- Fixed route services: Where hauliers have regular and recurring delivery routes that coincide with existing Felix routes and will allow Felix to add pallets
- Near-term movements: Where ad hoc food offers can be added to the platform and then picked up by logistics providers 4–24 hours ahead, in a more reactive way

items.body:
Aldi has begun handling fruit and vegetables at its Bardon Distribution Centre in Leicestershire, as the UK’s largest automated warehouse moves into its next phase of operation. The first pallets of produce, including ginger and avocados, were delivered to the site on Wednesday 16th September, with the first outbound pallet the following day.
The start of fresh produce operations follows the launch of operations at Bardon in May 2026. The UK’s biggest discounter has invested more than £500m in the site, which forms part of Aldi’s £1.6bn investment in Britain during 2026 and 2027. The facility is also the lowest carbon density warehouse across the Aldi South Group, with 19,000 solar panels installed on the roof.
Once fully operational in 2027, during peak periods more than 1.5 million kilograms of fruit and vegetables will move through the 1.3million square foot site daily and more than 6,000 pallets of fresh produce will depart the Bardon Distribution Centre every day bound for Aldi stores across the UK.
The latest automated technology being used at the site, delivered by technology partner Cimcorp, will help Aldi move fresh produce through the site more efficiently, while maintaining the different temperatures required to maintain freshness and shelf life of products including salad leaves, bananas and soft fruit.
The investment will add capacity to Aldi’s distribution network as the supermarket works towards its long-term ambition of operating 1,500 UK stores. Once fully operational, the site will employ around 1,000 colleagues and have the capacity to handle nearly seven million pallets annually.
The fresh produce operation at Bardon spans three dedicated temperature-controlled areas, with chilled storage for products like apples and carrots, and a specialist banana room. In the chilled chamber, pallets are moved into high-bay racking until they’re needed to go to stores, then automated shuttles will call them down for dispatch.
As the UK’s third biggest retailer of fresh produce, Aldi sells an average of 2.2 billion fruit and vegetables every year, including over 300 million bananas, 80 million apples and 160 million potatoes. In July 2026 alone, Aldi sold 2,250 tonnes of British apples making it the biggest customer of domestic apple growers. The retailer also has a target to increase the number of portions of fruit and veg sold by 14% by the end of 2027.
Jonathan Heaton, regional managing director for Bardon, at Aldi UK, said: “The start of fresh produce operations at Bardon is a proud moment for everyone involved in this project and marks a step change in how we serve our customers. Fresh produce is a vital part of our customers’ shopping, yet it presents one of the most complex challenges in grocery logistics, with products needing to move quickly and efficiently from suppliers to stores to maintain freshness. The technology we’ve implemented with Cimcorp allows us to handle enormous volumes while maintaining the precision and care that fresh products demand.
“This investment is about more than efficiency. By reducing the cost of moving products from our suppliers to our stores, we can continue to deliver the lowest prices on the market while ensuring customers always find fresh, high-quality fruit and vegetables on our shelves. As operations build over the coming weeks, Bardon will play an increasingly important role in Aldi’s supply chain, supporting our continued growth across the UK.”
Mikko Kumpulainen, key account manager at Cimcorp, said: “Fresh food logistics present unique operational challenges that require specialised technology and expertise. This distribution centre demonstrates how intelligent automation can manage high volumes while maintaining the flexibility needed for a complex grocery environment.
“Our automation allows Aldi to respond more effectively to changing demand patterns while supporting long-term growth. Ultimately, the goal is simple: ensuring high-quality fresh products are available for consumers whenever they visit their local store.”

items.title: Ready for the rush | In focus: Winter remedies
items.summary: As autumn approaches, independent retailers need to make sure their winter remedies range is in place before the season of coughs, colds and sore throats really kicks in. For most independent stores, that means concentrating on a manageable core range rather than trying to cover… This story continues at Ready for the rush | In focus: Winter remedies Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
For most independent stores, that means concentrating on a manageable core range rather than trying to cover every option. Trusted brands, strong availability and products that address different shopper needs should take priority.
Changing needs
Elizabeth Hughes-Gapper, senior brand manager at Jakemans, says the amount of space given to the category depends on store size, but that all retailers should make sure it is easy to shop and well stocked throughout the winter. “As retailers move into autumn and winter, it’s important to adapt the over-the-counter (OTC) fixture to reflect changing shopper needs, with a strong range of trusted winter remedies available ahead of the seasonal peak,” she says.
Alongside established cough and throat products, Hughes-Gapper recommends offering sugar-free options and different flavours to provide a wider choice.
Brand recognition has an important role to play when shoppers choose OTC products. Research from the PAGB Self-Care Census 2025, cited by Jakemans, shows that 93% of branded OTC buyers use brand names to help them decide which products to buy. Jakemans says it is the UK’s number one cough and throat lozenge brand, according to Kantar data to 22 March.
Rival brand Halls also points to familiarity as an important part of the buying decision. Susan Nash, trade communications manager at Mondelēz International, says retailers should cover both menthol clearing and gentler soothing options.
Accessible options
Data from market analyst Nielsen, supplied by Mondelēz, shows Halls as the leading “relief candy” brand in the UK. Its range features Halls Mentholyptus, including Extra Strong and sugar free variants, alongside Halls Soothers.
Singles are particularly important in this sub-category, Mondelēz says, reflecting shoppers’ need for an easy-to-buy product when symptoms strike.
Visibility is as important as range, suppliers argue, with winter remedies needing a clear home in the healthcare fixture. But secondary siting can help retailers pick up extra sales, they add. “Dual-siting, such as merchandising throat lozenges both within the healthcare aisle and near the till, makes products easier to find and encourages impulse purchases,” says Hughes-Gapper.
This is particularly useful for products such as throat lozenges and cough sweets, where purchases may be prompted by an immediate need rather than a planned shop. Promotions can add visibility, but Jakemans argues they work best alongside clear signposting, good availability and simple symptom-led merchandising.
Secondary space
The category is also broadening. Sugar-free products are becoming more prominent, while new flavours give shoppers more choice within familiar formats. Jakemans, for example, has added Sugar Free Summer Berries to its permanent range and is preparing to introduce Blood Orange & Warm Spice in September.
For independents, though, the priority is straightforward: have the core winter lines in place before demand builds, keep trusted products easy to find, and use secondary space where possible to turn a pressing need into a quick purchase.

items.body:
Following the release of Kingsfisher’s figures for the six months ending 31 July 2026; Jake Kendrick, retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers his view: “Kingfisher’s H1 FY2026/27 results demonstrate underlying resilience, with the group upgrading its profit before tax guidance (PBT) despite weaker sales amidst, a challenging home-improvement market with subdued consumer demand. Group l-f-l big-ticket spending (kitchen, bathroom and storage products) declined 4.6%, underscoring continued pressure on household budgets, weaker housing activity across Europe and more cautious discretionary DIY spending. Despite this, PBT guidance has been upgraded to £595-635m as gross margins have improved, and costs have been carefully controlled. With CEO Thierry Garnier stepping down; the incoming CEO will inherit momentum in trade and digital but must tackle ongoing weakness in Kingfisher’s core retail proposition.
“B&Q remains under strain. Q2 LFL performance was marginally better than Q1, as heatwaves boosted demand for cooling appliances and outdoor furniture, however, it still has a considerable way to go. Online and TradePoint continued to support B&Q’s offering, with online sales up 19.3% and TradePoint sales up 0.2% to £490m, signalling a shift in demand towards more specialised, service-led propositions and convenient fulfilment. B&Q is facing a threat amid intensifying competition for trade customers, with Wickes’ TradePro sales growing 5% year-on-year in H1 2025/26 (six months ending 27 June 2026), underlining Wickes’ strengthening trade proposition and raising the bar for B&Q to improve availability, service and convenience
“Screwfix shows what a sharper proposition can deliver, even in a challenging market, supported by its trade focus, digital convenience and store expansion, with 16 new stores planned for FY2026/27. Seasonal demand also contributed, with l-f-l seasonal sales up 16.3%, highlighting Screwfix’s ability to capture weather-driven demand through its trade-focused, convenience-led model. Its proposition has also resonated internationally. Screwfix delivered 48% store l-f-l growth in France, reinforcing that trade-led missions and convenience are the most dependable sources of growth. Kingfisher must draw on Screwfix’s success by enhancing its other retail banners with greater product availability and frictionless fulfilment, enabling each retailer to build on its individual strengths and capture more demand.”

items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. New Look, M&S, Sainsbury’s, Oxfam and Circle-8 today announce The Circuit, a new collaborative model bringing together retailers, textile recovery partners, automated sorting, recyclers, digital innovators and manufacturers to help build new circular textile value chains and transform UK generated post-consumer textiles into future circular raw materials. The first phase of the initiative will focus […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
New Look, M&S, Sainsbury’s, Oxfam and Circle-8 today announce The Circuit, a new collaborative model bringing together retailers, textile recovery partners, automated sorting, recyclers, digital innovators and manufacturers to help build new circular textile value chains and transform UK generated post-consumer textiles into future circular raw materials. The first phase of the initiative will focus on testing, learning and developing the operational frameworks needed to support future scale-up.
In 2024, approximately 1.4 million tonnes of post-consumer textiles were generated across the UK, reinforcing the need for greater investment in the infrastructure required to recover, reuse and recycle valuable textile resources. It’s estimated nearly half of this is made up of non-reusable textiles1, highlighting the need for new solutions to recover and recycle textiles at scale. Demand for recycled textile materials is growing, but the systems needed to create them from post-consumer textiles are still emerging. The Circuit has been established to close that gap.
The Circuit is designed to create new pathways through which UK generated non-reusable end-of-use textiles can be recovered, sorted and pre-processed into input materials for the existing and emerging fibre to fibre recycling industry. By bringing together organisations from across the value chain, The Circuit aims to create the scale, consistency and commercial conditions needed accelerate future textile to textile recycling viability. The initiative also supports the broader UK economy by enabling job creation and manufacturing. Automated sorting and pre-processing, close to the source of where textiles that have reached end of use are generated and turned into feedstock for regional and global supply chains.
The partnership supports the development of both mechanical and chemical recycling processes capable of transforming UK generated post-consumer textiles into raw materials for regional and global textile manufacturing. By creating multiple routes to market and products for recovered materials, participating retailers will help shape the value chains that support future circular materials.
Circle-8, the development company behind The Circuit, is developing the infrastructure, partnerships and commercial frameworks required to connect post-consumer textile recovery with future circular material supply. This includes the development of Automated Textile Sorting and Pre-processing facilities, which create feedstock for existing and emerging textile recyclers.
The first phase of The Circuit will begin in January 2027, bringing together retailers and partners at Oxfam’s site in Batley, Yorkshire. The initial phase will focus on automated textile sorting, combined with developing reporting frameworks to improve traceability, identifying circular material opportunities, building relationships with recyclers and exploring operational models that could support further scaling of the initiative. Oxfam will play a crucial role in separating the reusable and non-reusable textiles and operating the automated textile sorting equipment, building on its longstanding expertise in textile recovery and reuse.
Lynda Petherick, chief executive officer at New Look, said: “Building a more circular fashion industry requires collaboration right across the value chain. The Circuit gives retailers an opportunity to play an active role in developing the systems that could turn non-reusable textiles already in circulation into the raw materials of the future. For New Look, this is about looking at how we can help create more resilient, circular supply chains over the longer term. We’re pleased to be part of The Circuit, to help demonstrate what can be achieved at scale.”
Katharine Beacham, head of sustainability & materials in Fashion, Home & Beauty at M&S, said: “At M&S, we believe the most sustainable clothing is clothing that is worn and loved for longer. Through Plan A for Another Life, we have an ambition to give 5 million items Another Life by 2030 through rewear, repair, resale and recycling. However, when textiles reach the end of their usable life, we need better solutions to recover and recycle the materials they contain. The Circuit is an important step forward, bringing together organisations from across the retail industry to help create viable routes for non-reusable textiles and support a more circular future for fashion.”
Ben Smith, managing director of Sainsbury’s Tu Clothing, said: ”Creating a more circular future for textiles will take collaboration and innovation across the whole industry. The Circuit is an exciting opportunity to work alongside partners from across the value chain to explore how post-consumer textiles generated here in the UK can be given a new life as valuable raw materials. For Tu at Sainsbury’s, it’s about learning, testing practical solutions and helping shape a more circular textiles economy for the future.”
Rachel Cosgrove-Pearce, retail director at Oxfam, said: “Oxfam has been giving clothes a second life for almost 80 years, and our experience tells us that keeping clothing in use for as long as possible is one of the most effective ways to reduce fashion’s impact on our planet. But we also urgently need better solutions for textiles that can no longer be worn or reused. Developing the infrastructure to recover valuable fibres from end-of-use textiles is an important part of building a fashion system that uses fewer virgin resources and creates less environmental harm, and The Circuit brings together the expertise and investment needed to move this forward at scale. We’re proud to be playing our part, building on Oxfam’s long history of textile recovery and our work at Batley.”
Cyndi Rhoades, CEO and co-founder of Circle-8 Textile Ecosystems said: The retailers who help build circular textile value chains today will be best positioned to influence and benefit from them tomorrow. Through The Circuit, we’re powering the relationships, infrastructure and commercial frameworks needed to make that possible. No one organisation can create a circular textile value chain alone, and we look forward to welcoming others to The Circuit.

The findings point to a fast-changing market, as SMEs look for more efficient ways to move money across borders. The report, based on a survey of SMEs across 11 countries, suggests the market could […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Nine in 10 (91%) small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) trading internationally are set to switch their current cross-border payment provider in the next two years, according to Mastercard’s new Money in Motion report, compiled by Bain & Company. The findings point to a fast-changing market, as SMEs look for more efficient ways to move money across borders.
The report, based on a survey of SMEs across 11 countries, suggests the market could look very different by 2028, as competition intensifies in a fast-growing sector. The overall B2B cross-border payments market is set to grow by 51%, from $31.7 trillion in 2024 to $47.8 trillion by 2032.2 Against that backdrop, smaller specialist providers are projected to become the leading choice for SMEs’ cross-border payment needs. By then, 48% are expected to choose a fintech as their main provider, up from 30% in 2025, while 28% are expected to select a bank, compared with 42% in 2025.
The research shows that SME priorities are changing. Trust (35%) and speed (34%) are now the biggest considerations when selecting a cross-border payment provider, with cost and transparency close behind at 28% each. Among SMEs that have recently changed providers, two in three (67%) say faster transactions and more reliable settlements were the driving force. Once selected, trust remains the strongest anchor for loyalty in an increasingly fluid market.
More than nine in 10 (92%) SMEs surveyed already use multiple payment providers, showing that many are spreading their business across different partners to meet their cross-border payment needs.
“SMEs are rethinking what they need from cross-border payments. They are using more providers, comparing options more closely and becoming more willing to switch. For banks and fintechs, that creates a clear opportunity to win and keep their business by delivering the speed, trust and transparency SMEs now expect,” says Pratik Khowala, Global Head of Transfer Solutions, Mastercard.
SMEs are also looking beyond the payment itself. The report shows that they want more visibility, control 
Pratik Khowala continues: “Banks and fintechs cannot afford to treat cross-border payments as a back-office service. For SMEs, it is becoming a test of whether a provider understands their business. Those that keep pace can build deeper relationships. Those that do not risk losing not just payment volumes, but the wider SME relationship.”
How SME money movement priorities vary across markets
- In Indonesia and India, SMEs are among the most likely to shop around, with 34% and 29%, respectively,using at least four providers, compared with an average of 19% across the countries surveyed.
- In the UK, transparency is critical forbuilding loyalty, with 45% saying clear pricing makes them more likely to choose or stay with a provider, compared with 38% globally.
- In the US, 44% say real-time updates on payment status would increase their loyalty to a provider or make them more likely to use more of its services, compared with 32% globally.
- SMEs in Brazil are the most proactive in enhancing their cross-border payments, with six in 10 (60%) exploring additional tools, compared with a global average of 48%.
Joe Lischwe, financial services partner at Bain & Company, comments: “As SMEs expand internationally, they are building more relationships with customers, suppliers and partners across borders, and that is changing what they need from payment providers. Trust remains the anchor, but the fundamentals of the payment experience like reliability, transparency and efficiency increasingly need to simply work. The winners will be those that combine that trusted foundation with greater visibility, control and flexibility as their customers’ needs evolve.”
Racing all over the world
Mastercard has teamed up with the McLaren Mastercard 
The collaboration has resulted in a new film showing Mastercard’s technology in action, with an end-to-end cross-continental payment going head-to-head with the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1® Team’s fastest-ever pit stop of 1.8 seconds, set in 2023. Mastercard recorded a similar milestone in March, when a payment from the US to the Philippines took just under one second.
Laura Bowden, chief financial officer, McLaren Racing, comments: “Every fraction of a second matters to us on track, and that same discipline extends to how we run the business behind the scenes. We work with partners and suppliers across the world, so payments need to move quickly, reliably and with as little friction as possible.”
McLaren uses Airwallex to support its cross-border payment needs. Airwallex, in turn, connects to Mastercard Move, leveraging its global payout network to help facilitate fast, reliable and transparent payments for its customers.
Mastercard Move enables banks, fintechs and other payment providers – and their customers – to send and receive funds quickly, securely and transparently. Built on Mastercard’s trusted card and non-card networks, it supports domestic and international transfers across more than 200 countries and territories and in over 150 currencies, connecting to bank accounts, digital wallets, cards and cash endpoints.

items.body:
Boots, the UK’s leading health, wellness and beauty retailer, is making its TikTok Shop debut; bringing customers even more ways to shop its unrivalled beauty ranges online.
Launching on 28 September, Boots’ TikTok ‘Shopfront’ will pilot with a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products from ranges including No7 Pro Artist, Good Intent and Prime Forever. Further Boots brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
As TikTok Shop reports a 55% growth* on LIVE shopping sales, Boots’ debut marks an important step in how the retailer is reaching new and younger customers through emerging shopping channels and social platforms.
Paula Bobbett, chief digital and data officer at Boots, said: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.
“This is an important step in creating a more connected Boots shopping experience. It brings inspiration and purchase closer together, while giving customers the reassurance that they are buying directly from Boots, who they know and trust.”
The launch forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bringing beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, Boots aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop.
Emily Caine, head of beauty at TikTok Shop, said: “We’re delighted to welcome Boots to TikTok Shop. The arrival reflects how discovery commerce is changing the way millions of people find and shop the products they love right in their For You Feed. Beauty is one of TikTok Shop UK’s strongest and fastest-growing categories, and welcoming the UK’s most iconic high street beauty destination to our platform takes that to a new level. We can’t wait to see them embrace new formats like LIVE Shopping to build real-time connections and create entertaining shopping experiences for a whole new generation of customers.”
The official launch on 28 September will be supported by a live shopping event featuring No7 products, allowing customers to discover and shop products seamlessly through LIVE shopping sessions, while benefiting from exclusive launch offers.
The launch is being delivered in partnership with THG Ingenuity, a leading SaaS technology and operations platform for global ecommerce, with THG Commerce and THG Fulfil managing the TikTok Shop set up, LIVE shopping, social commerce experience and fulfilment.

items.body:
Asda is helping customers save at the pumps with the return of its popular fuel saving offer for Rewards users.
Customers who spend £40 or more in a single in-store transaction between 23rd September and 14th October will receive a 5p-per-litre fuel coupon in their Asda Rewards app, redeemable on a single fuel purchase until 31st October at participating Asda filling sites.
The offer could save driver up to £3 each time they fill up a typical 60-litre family car and is available at 262 participating Asda and Asda Express sites offering Asda-branded fuel.
Asda has brought back its fuel saving offer at a time when family budgets are under growing pressure from rising living costs.
The company’s monthly Income Tracker, which measures how much money households have left after paying taxes and essential bills, showed spending power growth slowed to 3.4% last month – the weakest level since March.
Rachel Eyre, chief customer officer at Asda, said: “The weekly shop and the cost of filling up the car are two of the biggest everyday expenses for many households. Customers told us how much they valued this Rewards offer when we ran it earlier this year. We’re pleased to bring it back as part of our continued investment to help keep the cost of feeding and fuelling the family down.”
Asda has continued to invest in keeping fuel and food prices in check for customers. Independent comparisons by Which? and The Grocer consistently recognising it as the UK’s cheapest full-range supermarket for groceries.
Customers can find full terms and conditions, including participating stores, on Asda.com and in the Asda Rewards app.
